events.title: Oppai Cats (girl garage band from Hiroshima) live in Berlin
Escapism Series, Part I
events.description:
Who’s been there? You spend twenty minutes tying the cleanest, prettiest gote of your life… and the person in ropes looks at you, shrugs, and casually wiggles themselves out like it was never that serious. Humbling. Kind of funny. And devinately annoying. 
This workshop leans directly into that irony: shibari is often not inherently inescapable. So what happens when we stop pretending it does? Escapism is a lab-based, curious, slightly mean-spirited exploration of tying specifically for the purpose of not being able to get out. Not decorative rope. Not “it’ll probably hold.” Rope designed to trap, frustrate, and quietly ruin someone’s confidence in their escape talent. 
Part I: July 29th, 2026, 8-10.30pm CEST
Part II: August 5th, 2026, 7-9.30pm CEST 
We’ll fuck around with:

Minimal rope vs. obscene amounts of rope
Simple ideas pushed way too far
Predicaments that look stupid until you’re inside them
Mean little concepts that rely more on physics, leverage, and bad choices than pretty patterns
What if the smartest escape route becomes the worst option?
What if struggling actively makes things harder?
What if the tie isn’t complex at all — just deeply unfair?

Expect experiments. Some will work. Some will fail hilariously.

events.description: TORSTEN GOODS MEETS ATRIN MADANI «YACHTROCK & WESTCOAST» FEAT : Till Sahm-Björn Werra-Magro Wenn der unverwechselbare Sound der amerikanischen Westküste auf zwei herausragende Stimmen trifft, ist ein besonderer Konzertabend garantiert. Torsten Goods meets Atrin Madani steht für geschmeidige Grooves, virtuose Gitarrenklänge und harmonischen Gesang im Stil von Yacht Rock und Westcoast . Freuen Sie sich auf Songs und Klassiker im Geiste von Steely Dan, Michael McDonald, Toto und den Doobie Brothers – mit viel Spielfreude und sommerlichem Flair. Ein Abend voller entspannter Kalifornien-Vibes, erstklassiger Musiker und zeitloser Songs – perfekt für alle Fans von Soul, Jazz und dem legendären Westcoast-Sound. Torsten Goods ist einer von Deutschlands besten und erfolgreichsten Jazz-Gitarristen und Jazz-Pop/Soul-Sängern, kurz: der „deutsche George Benson“ (SZ). Der 44-jährige ist außerdem deutscher Musikautorenpreisträger und wurde für seine sechs bisherigen Solo-Alben, die meisten davon beim renommierten Jazzlabel ACT, zweimal für den Echo Jazznominiert. Sein letztes Album „Soul Searching“ stieg mit Platz 2 in die Media Control Jazz Charts im September 2023 ein. events.title: Why the Sex Isn’t Working (and What to Do About It), Part II: Fun
events.description:
A three-part series for couples and polycules, exploring the most common places where sex breaks down, and how to rebuild with intention, honesty, and skill. 
Grounded in sex therapy and informed by kink-aware, queer-inclusive practice, this series looks at sex not as an isolated act, but as something shaped by conflict, connection, and relationship. 
July 16th: Part 1 – Fight
When sex isn’t working, it’s often not about sex. 
The first part of the series looks at the conflicts, tensions, and relational patterns that block desire and connection. We’ll explore how resentment, misaligned expectations, communication breakdowns, and unspoken needs show up in intimate spaces. 
You’ll learn how to identify the actual fight you’re having (hint: it’s rarely about the surface issue), and how to engage conflict in a way that creates connection instead of distance, and safety instead of resentment. We’ll work with tools for tenderness, empathy, and staying present in difficult conversations, negotiation, and boundary setting. 
July 30th: Part 2 – Fun
Before sex can work, the relationship needs to feel alive. 
When everything becomes logistical, tense, or goal-oriented, intimacy often follows suit. This workshop focuses on the role of play, fun, lightness, and connection outside of sex, and how their absence can quietly erode desire. 
We’ll explore how partners lose access to shared joy, and what it takes to rebuild it. What creates a sense of “us”? How do playfulness, curiosity, and mutual enjoyment show up in everyday interactions? And how can you reintroduce them without it feeling forced or performative? 
This session is about widening the lens: seeing sex as something that grows out of the overall tone of a relationship, not something that can be fixed in isolation. 
August 13th: Part 3 – Fuck
Once conflict is addressed and connection is alive, how do we actually do sex in a way that works? 
This workshop focuses on the experience of sex itself: arousal, pacing, communication during intimacy, and the role of play within sex. We’ll explore how to move away from scripts and expectations, and toward something more responsive, collaborative, and alive. 
What makes sex feel fun, engaging, and connected in the moment? How can we understand and embrace each other’s sexual blueprints? And how do we navigate mismatched desire, shifting arousal, or things not going according to plan? 
Expect honest conversations about bodies, variability, and the realities of sex, along with tools to build attunement, flexibility, and shared enjoyment. This is where the pieces come together: not perfect sex, but sex that actually works for the people having it. 
What to expect

A structured, three-part approach: conflict (Fight), relational connection (Fun), and sexual experience (Fuck)
Real-time conversations and exercises with your partner(s)
Insight into how non-sexual dynamics (resentment, disconnection, routine) shape sexual difficulties
Tools for navigating difficult conversations, rebuilding connection, and shifting relational patterns
Exploration of play, curiosity, and responsiveness – both in relationships and in sex
Honest, practical discussion of how sex actually works and how to take agency

Who it’s for

LGBTQIA+ couples and polycules feeling stuck, frustrated, or disconnected in their sex lives
People who want to work on things actively — not just get information and techniques
Those open to reflecting on their role in relational and sexual dynamics
Kink-aware, queer, and non-normative folks looking for inclusive, applicable frameworks

events.title: Three Of Seven
events.description:
Three of the seven continents of our planet contributed one musician each to the creation of the international jazz trio, Three of Seven. Europe is represented by Czech guitarist Libor Šmoldas, distant Australia by double bassist Sam Zerna, and North America by drummer Jesse Simpson, originally from California. What connects all three is the jazz mecca of New York, the city where Sam Zerna lives, Jesse Simpson lived and studied at the Manhattan School of Music, and where Libor Šmoldas regularly goes to perform and record.

You can look forward to a balanced combination of jazz standards and original compositions by all three members of Three of Seven. The music of the trio is full of improvisation, joy of playing and, last but not least, instrumental mastery, which is always in the service of melody and musicality. Due to the different cultures and musical backgrounds from which Libor, Sam and Jesse come, the resulting style is very varied and at the same time harmonious, linked by a common love of jazz history and an open approach to improvisation.

Libor Šmoldas is our leading jazz guitarist. Among the world clubs where he performs, there are Ronnie Scotts, Pizza Express, Smalls, Iridium, Blue Note, Birdland, Deer Head Inn, B flat, Porgy and Bess and Bennetts Lane. He played and recorded with world musicians such as George Mraz, Jeff Ballard, Sam Yahel, Bobby Watson, Adam Nussbaum, James Morrison, Brian Charette, Gregory Hutchinson, Jon Faddis and Jay Anderson. In the Czech Republic, he has collaborated with the complete top of jazz, including, for example, Ondřej Pivec, Robert Balzar and David Dorůžka. He has released eleven albums under his own name and a number of others as a bandmate. The Czech and international press agree on his high qualities and leading position among European jazz guitarists.

Samuel Zerna is an Australian bass player based in New York. In addition to Australia and the USA, he has performed throughout Europe, the U.K., China and New Zealand. Samuel has performed with leading New York musicians such as Will Vinson, Michael Mayo, Mike Moreno, Ben Eunson, Chris Cheek and Rogerio Boccato at venues such as Smalls Jazz Club, Mezzrow, the 55 Bar, the Kennedy Center, Jazz at Lincoln Center Shanghai, the Southbank Center London et al.  

Jesse Simpson is a drummer originally from California. He was a student of the legendary drummer Donald "Duck" Bailey, in 2007 he moved to New York where he graduated from the Manhattan School of Music. He has performed on the New York stage with Joe Lovano, John Abercrombie, Chris Cheek, Brian Charette and many others. Since 2022, he lives in the Czech Republic and continues to perform mainly on European stages.

events.title: Digital Independence Day
events.description:
Eventpate: uhuspecht

Let’s DID it! @ c-base – Linux-Special

Am ersten Sonntag des Monats auf die gute Seite wechseln!

Beim Digital Independence Day unterstützen wir dich dabei, deine digitale Autonomie zurückzugewinnen – gemeinsam und Schritt für Schritt. Ob von X zu Mastodon, von Google Chrome zu Firefox oder von Windows zu Linux: Wir helfen dir beim Wechsel zu freien und datenschutzfreundlichen Alternativen.

Dieses Mal dreht sich vieles um Linux und freie Software. In drei verständlichen Vorträgen erfährst du, was der DIDay ist, wie Linux funktioniert und wie sich Programme dort mithilfe eines Paketmanagers installieren und aktuell halten lassen.

Programm

14:00–14:15 Uhr – Ankommen
In Ruhe eintreffen, etwas trinken und einen Platz suchen.

14:15–14:30 Uhr – Was ist der DIDay?
Ein kurzer Einstieg: Worum geht es beim Digital Independence Day und was erwartet dich heute?

14:30–14:40 Uhr – Pause

14:40–15:10 Uhr – Was ist Linux?
Eine verständliche Einführung in das freie Betriebssystem und seine Möglichkeiten.

15:10–15:20 Uhr – Pause

15:20–15:35 Uhr – Was ist ein Paketmanager?
Wie lassen sich Programme unter Linux einfach installieren und aktuell halten?

Ab 15:35 Uhr – Offenes DIDay-Programm
Beratung, praktische Unterstützung und gemeinsamer Austausch rund um Linux, freie Software und digitale Selbstbestimmung.

Du kannst auch später dazukommen oder nur einzelne Programmpunkte besuchen.

Vielleicht möchtest du außerdem einen E-Mail-Dienst mit mehr Privatsphäre ausprobieren? Oder du möchtest bei einem Kaffee mehr über digitale Alternativen erfahren, die unsere Demokratie stärken und eine nachhaltige, selbstbestimmte Teilhabe ermöglichen?

Dann lass uns gemeinsam loslegen!

Es gibt Tee, Kaffee, Snacks und natürlich Cookies. Die Teilnahme ist kostenlos und Vorkenntnisse sind nicht erforderlich. Bring gern deinen Laptop, dein Smartphone oder ein anderes Gerät mit.

Der Zugang und der Veranstaltungsraum sind barrierefrei.

Gastgeberin ist die c-base. Mit dabei sind außerdem das Projekt Digital-Zebra (VÖBB), Topio, der kleindatenverein, Anoxinon e. V., Computertruhe e. V. und Möckernkiez e. V.

Gemeinsam mehr erreichen

Diese Veranstaltung ist Teil eines Netzwerks aus mehreren Organisationen und Initiativen in Berlin. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig mit Wissen, Erfahrung und praktischer Hilfe. Uns alle verbindet der Wunsch, Wissen zu teilen, voneinander zu lernen und solidarisch zusammenzuarbeiten.

Der DIDay bildet dafür den gemeinsamen Rahmen. Zusammen setzen wir uns für digitale Selbstbestimmung und nachhaltige digitale Strukturen ein.

events.title: Escapism Series, Part II
events.description:
Who’s been there? You spend twenty minutes tying the cleanest, prettiest gote of your life… and the person in ropes looks at you, shrugs, and casually wiggles themselves out like it was never that serious. Humbling. Kind of funny. And devinately annoying. 
This workshop leans directly into that irony: shibari is often not inherently inescapable. So what happens when we stop pretending it does? Escapism is a lab-based, curious, slightly mean-spirited exploration of tying specifically for the purpose of not being able to get out. Not decorative rope. Not “it’ll probably hold.” Rope designed to trap, frustrate, and quietly ruin someone’s confidence in their escape talent. 
Part I: July 29th, 2026, 8-10.30pm CEST
Part II: August 5th, 2026, 7-9.30pm CEST 
We’ll fuck around with:

Minimal rope vs. obscene amounts of rope
Simple ideas pushed way too far
Predicaments that look stupid until you’re inside them
Mean little concepts that rely more on physics, leverage, and bad choices than pretty patterns
What if the smartest escape route becomes the worst option?
What if struggling actively makes things harder?
What if the tie isn’t complex at all — just deeply unfair?

Expect experiments. Some will work. Some will fail hilariously.

Twisted Games - Exploring the Subtleties of Sadism
events.description:
What does it mean to be a little mean? How can sadism become playful, connective, attentive, or even tender? 
This workshop invites participants to explore the quieter, subtler, and more personal expressions of sadism beyond intensity alone. Together, we will investigate how teasing, tension, anticipation, discomfort, control, humour, and unusual impulses can support play, intimacy, and connection in ways that feel authentic to you. 
Caritia will guide participants through discussion, reflection, and collaborative exploration around the topic of s/m, encouraging curiosity, communication, and personal agency within play. Participants will be invited to experiment with one or two practical exercises and playful frameworks, exploring how different approaches to sadism can shift dynamics, sensation, trust, and relational presence. 
This workshop is less about performing a role and more about discovering your own language of play — whether mischievous, caring, awkward, intense, creative, or strange. Participants can expect a space centred on exploration, consent, experimentation, and finding new ways to connect through intentional play.

They will also dive deeper into uttering and processing sensations in impact play, and how intentions, consent, and setup have a huge impact (pun intended) on everyone’s mindset.

How well do you know your body? Frequently, within kink, intimacy, and body-based practices, this question comes up. It is not a prerequisite to know everything, as part of the play is discovering exactly this; however, if we wish to be intentional and caring within the plays and practices we participate in, what foundational knowledge might support us?

Together, participants will investigate how bodies communicate, respond, compensate, resist, soften, and connect through movement and touch. 
Through solo, partnered, and group-based exploration, participants will build greater body agency and self-knowledge, learning to recognise personal limits, habits, strengths, tensions, and desires. Caritia will offer practical tips and tricks on body mechanics, weight-sharing, posture, mobility, and the interconnection between our bodies and the bodily presence of others. 
Participants can expect to leave with tools for more intentional movement in rope and play, increased confidence in noticing and responding to their own bodies, and a deeper understanding of how collaborative learning and embodied awareness can enrich intimacy, trust, communication, care, and creativity.

Together, participants will explore the emotional, relational, physical, and imaginative aspects of moving between topping and bottoming, and what draws us toward different forms of expression at different times. 
Through guided discussion, reflective prompts, shared experiences, and playful exploration, we will nerd out about dynamics, desire, communication, embodiment, power, care, curiosity, and the flexibility that switching can offer within kink and intimacy. 

This space welcomes uncertainty, experimentation, contradiction, and growth. Whether you identify strongly as a switch, are switch-curious, or simply want to better understand the fluidity of play, participants can expect an environment centred on agency, self-knowledge, humour, collaboration, and connection.

events.description: A-Trane präsentiert: WOLFGANG HAFFNER SUMMER SPECIAL FEAT : Jakob Manz-Nils Kugelmann Zum Jubiläum lädt Wolfgang Haffner zu einem ganz besonderen Summer Special ins A-Trane ein. Gemeinsam mit langjährigen musikalischen Weggefährten wie Ulf Wakenius, Christopher Dell und Thomas Stieger, sowie den Shooting Stars Jakob Manz und Nils Kugelmann, präsentiert er musikalische Wegmarken einer einzigartigen Karriere . Das „Wolfgang Haffner Summer Special“ ist eine musikalische Feier – für Haffner selbst, für sein Publikum und für die verbindende Kraft des Jazz. Wolfgang Haffner Wolfgang Haffner zählt zu den herausragenden Persönlichkeiten des europäischen Jazz – ein Schlagzeuger von Weltformat, der in diesem Jahr beeindruckende 50 Jahre Bühnenpräsenz feiert. Mehr als 4000 Konzerte in über 100 Ländern, Mitwirkung auf rund 400 Alben, zwei ECHO Jazz- Auszeichnungen – Haffners musikalische Vita liest sich wie ein internationales Erfolgsmärchen. Ob mit Al Jarreau, Chaka Khan, Pat Metheny, Gregory Porter, Bill Evans oder Klaus Doldinger, ob mit Till Brönner, Hildegard Knef, Nils Landgren, Nightmares On Wax oder Die Fantastischen Vier – die Liste seiner Kollaborationen ist ebenso lang wie klangvoll. Sein unverkennbarer Stil, seine Vielseitigkeit und sein feines Gespür für Groove machen ihn zu einem der meistgefragten Schlagzeuger weltweit . Jakob Manz Der 2001 geborene Jakob Manz gilt als Shootingstar der deutschen Jazzszene. Manz ist bekannt für seine beeindruckende Technik und sein melodisch vielseitiges Saxophonspiel. Er begann schon als kleines Kind seine musikalische Ausbildung und studierte bereits als Schüler an der Hochschule für Musik und Darstellende Kunst in Stuttgart und wurde Mitglied des BuJazzO (Bundesjazzorchester). Manz ist bekannt für seine Arbeit mit verschiedenen Ensembles, darunter das Jakob Manz Project und die SWR Big Band. Manz arbeitet mit vielen nahmhaften Musikern zusammen und ist regelmäßig auf nationalen und internationalen Festivals und in Clubs zu sehen. Jakob Manz ist einer der vielversprechensden jungen Saxophonisten in Deutschland und Europa, der durch seine frischen und innovativen Ansätze heraussticht . Nils Kugelmann Gewichtiger Ton, packender Groove und dynamisches Zusammenspiel prägen die Musik von Nils Kugelmann. 2023 gewann der Münchner Kontrabassist den renommierten Nachwuchspreis der Jazzwoche Burghausen, die Süddeutsche Zeitung schreibt: „ Nils Kugelmann lässt jeden einzelnen Ton noch im höchsten Tempo definiert erklingen und macht so komplexe, weit für Improvisation offene Kompositionen unwiderstehlich und eingängig .“ Und die Jury des BMW Young Artist Jazz Award konstatiert: „ Schon jetzt einer der besten deutschen Bassisten .» Wolfgang Haffner – Drums Jakob Manz – Alto Saxophone Nils Kugelmann – Bass Wolfgang Haffner Foto©Migal Vanas Jakob-Manz-Foto©Gregor-Hohenberg Nils Kugelmann Foto©Uli-Neumann-Cosel

events.description:
FADFADA in Arabic, means "unburdening," or "heart-to-heart." The musical duo "Fadfada" weaves together original works, Arabic classical compositions, and beloved popular songs from the Middle East and North Africa, seeking to create an intimate and deeply personal musical language that spans the vastly different yet interconnected lives of its two members.

The duo features Nabil Arbaain, an oud player hailing from Damascus, Syria, and Hans Bilger, a double bassist and oud player from Brooklyn, New York. events.title: Carlota Flâneur
events.description:
Carlota Flâneur is a catalan singer-songwriter who will be playing her songs live in Berlin for the first time on Aug 23 at Donau115.

She debuted in 2020 with Brains, her first EP. Back then she already stood out for her capacity to combine brilliant melodies with raw, no-filter lyrics. Uncertainty, her first album, managed to broaden her sonic universe and consolidated her artistic view, filling it with colorful, warm and catchy tunes.

In 2024 Carlota released Relate, a single in which she joined forces with two of her favourite catalan artists: Núria Graham and Marta Knight, to deliver a polished, smooth and dreamy tune.

Flâneur wanted to further expand her colour palette, and so she did in her latest album, What my body wants. This album is a balanced mix of light and shadow, full of interesting textures and harmonies that are perfectly placed to elevate the catalan’s fully recognisable songwriting.

events.title: Piena
events.description: Piena writes songs for overthinkers. Her biggest dream is to write a perfect love song. Until then, she writes about longing, self-deception, and the darker sides of the psyche. A singer, songwriter, and aspiring multi-instrumentalist from Amsterdam, she grew up with classical music, trained as a jazz vocalist, and now makes pop music. At first, that was confusing, but now she feels most at home in the in-between space; her sound is both analog and electronic, her lyrics are often as light-hearted as they are tragic, and you never know for sure where the delusion ends and the irony begins.

events.description: Pepe Berns «Old and New Friends» Gratitude 60th Birthday Celebration Concerts TODAY : TRIO BLUR FEAT : SOPHIA GÜNST & YAKOU TRIBE SPECIAL GUESTS : WERNER NEUMANN & CHRISTOPH ADAMS Der seit 1994 in Berlin lebende Bassist und Professor für Jazz Kontrabass an der Hmt Leipzig Pepe Berns kann auf eine über 40jährige Karriere zurückblicken, die ihn von Köln über LA nach NY führte. Er arbeitete mit zahllosen Größen der internationalen und lokalen Jazzwelt. Nun feiert er an zwei Abenden seinen 60. Geburtstag in seinem Lieblings-Jazz Club „A-TRANE“ und hat hierfür viele seiner engsten Freunde und Wegbegleiter aus neuester Zeit und vergangen Tagen zu sich auf die Bühne eingeladen . Den ersten Abend (25.08.) beginnt er mit seinem jüngsten Projekt, dem Trio:Blur mit den talentierten Newcomern Emmanuel Walter (p) und Lucas Rauch (dr) und der wundervollen Sängerin Sophia Günst. Im zweiten Set wird er mit seinen Freunden Jan von Klewitz (sax), Kai Brückner (git) und Rainer Winch (Dr) mit der seit 25 Jahre aktiven Band „Yakou Tribe“ spielen und hat außerdem zwei weitere Mitstreiter der ersten Stunde gewinnen können: Werner Neumann (git) und Christoph Adams (p) Den zweiten Abend (26.08.) widmet Berns gleich drei wichtigen Stationen seines Lebens und lädt dazu den großartigen Pianisten Sebastian Weiss (CD Berns Köbberling Weiss 2003) ein, gefolgt von seinen Hamburger Freunden der einstigen Band „Nerd Network“ (CD 1999) Gabriel Coburger (sax) Buggy Braune (p) und Heinz Lichius. Als Abschluss des Abends wird das original besetzte „Jonas Schoen Quartett“ mit den letzt genannten Musikern zu hören sein. Ganz bestimmt endet dieser Abend in einer fulminanten Session . Eine Zeitreise durch die Dekaden und Stile des Jazz, vielfältige Besetzungen und wundervolle Solisten*innen.
